title: 2009 HMMT February Guts Problem 13
statement: How many ordered quadruples \((a, b, c, d)\) of four distinct numbers chosen from the set \(\{1,2,3, \ldots, 9\}\) satisfy \(b<a, b<c\), and \(d<c\) ?

solutions.text: Given any 4 elements \(p<q<r<s\) of \(\{1,2, \ldots, 9\}\), there are 5 ways of rearranging them to satisfy the inequality: prqs, psqr, qspr, qrps, and rspq. This gives a total of \(\binom{9}{4} \cdot 5=630\) quadruples.
